sections.content: How many people are "database administrators and web content technicians"?

45,155 people

were counted on the census as "database administrators and web content technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Database administrators and web content technicians administer, maintain and provide user support for databases and websites. They also assist in the design and development of databases and may monitor social media sites for posts and comments on behalf of companies.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "database administrators and web content technicians", 17.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "database administrators and web content technicians" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "database administrators and web content technicians" included:

  • IT user support technicians
  • air travel assistants
  • human resources and industrial relations officers

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "database administrators and web content technicians" there were a similar number of men and women (49.5% compared with 50.5%).

This means "database administrators and web content technicians" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, engineering and technology associate professionals".

Men made up 49.5% and women made up 50.5% of "database administrators and web content technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "database administrators and web content technicians" included:

  • other researchers, unspecified discipline
  • insurance underwriters
  • hotel and accommodation managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "database administrators and web content technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "database administrators and web content technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "database administrators and web content technicians", 10.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (76.4% compared with 23.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (88.3%) than self-employed (11.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
